ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A smooth quarter-circular track PQ is placed vertically, with its bottom end tangent to a horizontal conveyor belt. A small block $a$ with mass $m_{\mathrm{a}}=1\mathrm{kg}$ is released from rest at the highest point $P$ of the circular track. When it reaches the lowest point $Q$, it undergoes an elastic head-on collision with another small block $b$ of mass $m_{\mathrm{b}}=3\mathrm{kg}$ (the collision time is extremely short). It is known that the radius of the circular track is $R=0.8\mathrm{m}$, the length of the conveyor belt is $L=1.25m$, the conveyor belt rotates clockwise at a constant speed of $v=1\mathrm{m/s}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the small objects and the conveyor belt is $\mu=0.2$, and $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the force exerted by the small block $a$ on the circular track at the instant before the collision?
2. What is the maximum height that the small block $a$ can reach after the collision?
3. What is the time required for the small block $b$ to move from the left end to the right end of the conveyor belt?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertically placed smooth quarter-circle track, with the highest point labeled P and the lowest point labeled Q; the dashed lines show the horizontal and vertical radius relationship between the circle center O and P, Q, therefore the vertical height difference from P to Q is R. The track is tangent at point Q to the horizontal conveyor belt on the right, and the tangent direction is to the right along the conveyor belt. Small block a is at point P, and small block b is near Q, at the left end of the conveyor belt; the arrow above the conveyor belt indicates that its upper surface speed v is to the right, and the length of the conveyor belt is L. Reasoning: a slides from rest at P to Q, mechanical energy is conserved: m_a gR = (1/2)m_a u^2, so u = sqrt(2gR)=sqrt(2×10×0.8)=4 m/s. At the instant before reaching Q, the centripetal direction is vertically upward, there is N - m_a g = m_a u^2/R, therefore N = 1×10 + 1×16/0.8 = 30 N. The force of a on the track is equal in magnitude to the supporting force of the track on a, which is 30 N. The collision time is extremely short, ignore the conveyor belt friction. b is initially at rest, after the elastic head-on collision: v_a' = (m_a-m_b)/(m_a+m_b)·u = (1-3)/(1+3)×4 = -2 m/s, that is, a reverses direction and slides up along the track; v_b' = 2m_a/(m_a+m_b)·u = 2×1/4×4 = 2 m/s. The maximum height to which a rises after the collision is obtained from (1/2)m_a v_a'^2 = m_a gh, giving h = v_a'^2/(2g)=4/20=0.2 m. After the collision, b moves to the right at 2 m/s, while the upper surface speed of the conveyor belt is 1 m/s to the right, so b slides to the right relative to the conveyor belt, the friction force is to the left, the magnitude of acceleration is μg=0.2×10=2 m/s², taking rightward as positive then a_b=-2 m/s². The time to decelerate to the same speed as the conveyor belt, 1 m/s, is t1=(2-1)/2=0.5 s, and the displacement in this section is s1=(2+1)/2×0.5=0.75 m. The remaining distance L-s1=1.25-0.75=0.50 m, afterward it moves uniformly with the conveyor belt at 1 m/s, with time t2=0.50/1=0.5 s. The total time t=t1+t2=1.0 s.
